note: Hypothalamic hamartoma combined with mesoaxial polydactyly is the defining hallmark of Pallister-Hall syndrome, supporting its utility in discriminating PHS from other ciliopathies with endocrine deficiency.

evidence.text: The diagnosis of Pallister-Hall syndrome can be established in a proband with both hypothalamic hamartoma and mesoaxial polydactyly.

evidence.text: Pallister-Hall syndrome is classically characterized by the presence of a hypothalamic hamartoma and central polydactyly, alongside endocrine and pituitary abnormalities.

source.title: Pallister-Hall Syndrome Presenting in Adolescence - PMC - NIH
source.quote: Pallister-Hall syndrome (PHS) is an extremely rare syndrome of unknown prevalence with autosomal dominant inheritance due to GLI3 gene mutations classically characterized by the presence of a hypothalamic hamartoma and polydactyly.
